title: serving-runtime-daily-scratchpad-2026-03-24
content:
Daily scratchpad - quick brain dump (Ethan)
Date: 2026-03-24

Top of mind / goals for today:
- triage SRV-1423 (kv-cache eviction causing stale prefixes) — blocking canary rollout to prod-lite
- follow up on attention-kernel perf regression discovered on rtx-a100-pool-2 (p99 token time up ~12% vs baseline)
- finish small refactor to kernel selection heuristic to prefer fused-gemm for small batch sizes
- sync with Priya about telemetry gaps for continuous batching metrics

Notes / triage for SRV-1423:
- Reported: cache returning older kv-entries after scale-down + restart of worker (repro in staging)
- Steps to reproduce (staging):
  1) start canary with model=v1.3-quant, run steady stream (median seq=512) at 10 qps for 5m
  2) trigger scale-down (reduce desired replicas) -> kill one pod during shrink window
  3) resume traffic, hit prefix mismatch on ~0.7% of requests (observed in logs)
- Hypothesis: local in-memory cache not invalidating on reattach to shared storage; possible race in cache-sync code path (cache_manager.go: line ~214)
- Quick checks done: added logs to cache miss/hit counts, confirmed bump in stale-hit metric after restart
- Potential fixes: force refresh on worker start (safe), add per-worker version tag to kv entries and check at read (more robust)
- Next steps: publish triage notes to SRV-1423, assign a short-term hotfix (force refresh on init) + follow-up design for version tags
- Blockers: reproducer flaky on local minikube due to timings — rely on staging cluster reproducer (logs attached to ticket)

Attention kernel perf regression:
- Observed: nightly perf-run 2026-03-23 vs baseline (2026-03-16) shows p50 ~same, p95 +6%, p99 +12% for seq lengths >= 256 on A100 (driver: 525.85?)
- Recent change: merged PR #870 that added tiled attention fallback for long sequences (intended to help NV long-seq cases)
- Hypothesis A: kernel selection heuristic prefers tiled fallback for shapes where fused attention would be better due to micro-batching differences
- Hypothesis B: new fused kernel has alignment edge cases on certain batch shapes causing extra memcpy (check nvprof)
- Quick diagnostic plan:
  - reproduce locally on a100-sim VM with same driver, run microbench harness (bench/attention_bench.py) for shapes: (b=1..8, seq=128,256,512), compare kernels chosen and time
  - add detailed kernel selection logging in serving process (temporarily) to see path decisions
  - run nvprof/nsys on a selected run to see memcpy counts
- Priya to help instrument the selection logs; I'll take the nsys capture if we can reserve a slot on a100-pool-2

Kernel selection heuristic TODOs:
- refactor selection to be table-driven: inputs -> candidate kernels -> cost_estimate -> pick; cost_estimate should incorporate measured microbenchmarks (per-hardware) + estimate for memcpy overhead
- quick hack: prefer fused-gemm for batch_size <= 4 and seq <= 256 (empirically better in 3/3 tests) — implement as config override flag (runtime-config: kernel_overrides)
- longer term: build small nightly microbench that populates cost table per instance type and pushes to central config store

Observability gaps / telemetry:
- continuous-batching metrics: missing histogram of batch sizes per model; we only have aggregate tokens/sec and avg batch size
- add: batch_size distribution (buckets:1,2,3-4,5-8,9-16,17-32,32+) and per-route tagging
- KV-cache: add metric for 'stale_read' boolean tagged by model and worker_id
- Log sampling: increase sample rate for cache debug logs in staging for next 48h

Today
- 09:30 sync with Priya (instrumentation plan)
- 10:30 debug session with Liam to reproduce SRV-1423 on staging
- 14:00 perf repro + nsys capture (if access available)
- 16:00 quick PR to add startup cache refresh (hotfix)

Small reminders / notes to self:
- when adding hotfix, ensure we don't trigger stampede: add jittered refresh + backoff
- add a unit test for cache_manager restart path (simulate partial writes)
- record benchmark numbers in sheets: link to perf sheet (put id in ticket)

Open questions / discussion items:
- do we keep per-worker in-memory cache for faster reads or move to shared redis for stronger consistency? tradeoffs: latency vs consistency + infra cost
- estimate cost for running nightly microbench matrix across all queue types (rough calc: 4 hw types * 6 shapes * 10 iterations -> ~240 runs; each run ~2m -> 8h total) -> maybe run shard across machines

Scratchpad snippets (commands):
- reproduce nsys: export NSYS_NVTX=1 && nsys profile --output /tmp/nsys_run --capture-range=cudaProfilerApi -- python bench/attention_bench.py --model t5 --batch 4 --seq 512
- quick grep for cache log: kubectl logs -l app=serving --since=1h | grep "cache: stale" | wc -l

Done for now — will update after 10:30 triage.

-- Ethan
